references.text: Moses laid his hands on Joshua to appoint him to service, using the same laying-on-of-hands ritual that was used for the consecration of the Levites.
Laying of hands on the head of the sacrificial animal, symbolizing identification and transfer, parallel to Israel's laying of hands on the Levites.
Laying of hands at the peace offering, the same symbolic act as in the consecration of the Levites.
The elders of the congregation laid their hands on the sin offering, parallel to the people's representation through laying of hands on the Levites.
Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom when Moses laid his hands on him, showing the significance of laying on of hands for the transfer of service and authority.
The apostles laid their hands on the seven deacons at their appointment to service, a practice rooted in the consecration of the Levites.
The church in Antioch laid their hands on Barnabas and Saulus and sent them out to service, following the pattern of laying-on-of-hands rituals from the Old Testament.
Timothy received his spiritual gift through the laying on of hands by the council of elders, continuing the tradition from the consecration of the Levites.
Paul warns against being too hasty in laying on of hands, showing the continued significance of the ritual in the church.
Paul reminds Timothy of the spiritual gift he received through his laying on of hands, which connects to the consecration ritual in the Old Testament.
